analysis_method.step1_load_and_harmonize: pandas.read_csv on all 4 datasets; diabetes Glucose/BMI/BloodPressure zeros -> NaN BEFORE any drop; harmonized to columns [source, age, glucose, bmi, bp, target] (stroke bp = 'hypertension' binary proxy; heart glucose = fbs proxy True->140/False->90 and bmi unavailable; sleep bmi = BMI Category ordinal map and bp = systolic from 'sys/dia', glucose unavailable).
analysis_method.step2_unified_dataset: Per-source dropna(subset=['age','glucose','bmi','bp']), then stroke sampled to 1000 (random_state=42), then concat + reset_index. Heart (no BMI) and Sleep (no glucose) contribute 0 rows by the mandated rule.
analysis_method.step3_feature_engineering: glucose_bmi_ratio = glucose/(bmi+1); age_glucose_interaction = age*glucose/1000; bp_bmi_ratio = bp/(bmi+1); source_encoded = LabelEncoder(diabetes=0, stroke=1); 8-column candidate matrix; median fill applied (0 missing values remained).
analysis_method.step5_pca: PCA(n_components=3, random_state=42) fit on StandardScaler-transformed 8-feature candidate matrix
analysis_method.step7_model: LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42, C=1.0) on StandardScaler-transformed hybrid features, target = binary chronic condition indicator
analysis_method.step8_ranking: Coefficients ranked by absolute magnitude; saved coefficient table, selected feature list, 1x2 figure, and top coefficient

heart_disease_uci.reason: no BMI column -> fails base-biomarker drop rule

sleep_health.reason: no glucose column -> fails base-biomarker drop rule

interpretation: pca_component_3 has the largest |coefficient| (3.702301); its loadings are bmi +0.72 and glucose_bmi_ratio -0.54, i.e. a body-composition axis consistent with the strong negative bmi (-2.99) and age_glucose_interaction (-2.98) effects.

Among interpretable raw features, higher BMI, higher age*glucose interaction and higher bp/bmi ratio all lower the odds of the composite chronic-condition indicator (negative signs), while raw glucose and raw bp are positive but weaker.

Caveat: because 'bp' is semantically inconsistent across sources (diastolic mm Hg for diabetes vs binary 0/1 hypertension for stroke) and prevalence differs sharply (34% vs 5.4%), the PCA components and bp-related terms absorb cohort (source) structure; coefficients are associative, not causal, and in-sample metrics (acc 0.812, AUC 0.862) are not out-of-sample validated.

outputs.feature_coefficients.csv: rank, feature, coefficient, abs_coefficient (8 hybrid features, ranked by |coefficient|)
outputs.selected_features.csv: feature, feature_type (rfe_selected / pca_component), abs_coefficient (8 features in hybrid order)
outputs.feature_analysis.png: 1x2 figure: left = hybrid feature coefficients (sorted by |coef|), right = PCA explained variance (individual bars + cumulative line)
outputs.top_coefficient.txt: coefficient of the most important predictor (pca_component_3) = 3.702301
